_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Moore's law says chips double every 18 months.
beats.note: Gordon Moore says he never said that.

beats.name: Gordon Moore
beats.role: Then head of research and development at Fairchild Semiconductor. His paper ran in Electronics magazine on 19 April.

beats.note: He expected it to hold for at least ten years, reaching 65,000 components per circuit by 1975.

beats.text: In 1975 he changed it to two years.
beats.note: He said so at the IEEE International Electron Devices Meeting.

beats.context: The number everyone repeats. It was never Moore's.

beats.name: David House
beats.role: The Intel executive credited with the 18 months. He reasoned that chip performance would double about that often.

beats.text: The most famous number in computing belongs to someone else.

beats.line: Check the number, then the name.
